requirementsKey.network: Sandbox can download public data and npm packages
requirementsKey.webgl: Headless Playwright Chromium can create a WebGL2 context (proved by tests/e2e/webgl-smoke.spec.ts, added in S01)
requirementsKey.supabase: Docker daemon running, local Supabase running (npx supabase start), and .env.local has NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
requirementsKey.realtime: Local Supabase Realtime service healthy (npx supabase status lists it) with public access disabled for private channels in supabase/config.toml; verified by npm run check:realtime
requirementsKey.stripe: Stripe test-mode keys (STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET) in .env.local and Stripe CLI installed and logged in for webhook forwarding

tasks.title: Scaffold, PWA shell, quality gates
tasks.acceptance: Next.js 16.3.x (App Router) + TypeScript 6.0.x strict + Tailwind 4 builds with the exact versions pinned in CLAUDE.md (three, @react-three/fiber and @react-three/drei pinned without ^); npm scripts dev, build, start, typecheck, lint (ESLint CLI with jsx-a11y and no-console), format:check (Prettier), test (Vitest), e2e (Playwright, specs in tests/e2e) and budget, each with one passing sample; Playwright projects 'mobile-390' (390x844, touch) and 'desktop-1280'; tests/e2e/webgl-smoke.spec.ts proves headless Chromium creates a WebGL2 context, with launch flags documented in README; a shared e2e fixture fails any test on a console warning or error (PERF-1) and provides an axe check that fails on serious or critical violations (A11Y-2); PWA manifest via app/manifest.ts (name 'Clout City: NYC', short name 'Clout City'), icons, installable, locked mobile viewport; bottom tab layout correct at 390px; one overlay layer system (named layers, reserved safe zones for HUD, sheets, toasts and banners) with screenshot and bounding-box tests at 390 and 1280 proving no overlap (UX-1); structured logger in src/lib/log.ts; supabase CLI added as a devDependency and supabase/config.toml initialised (no running stack needed); .gitignore covers env files, build output, test artefacts and the geo download cache.

tasks.title: Data, copy, formatters, and store
tasks.acceptance: /data folders for items, premium, events, jobs, venues, landmarks, geo, zones, audio, config (including config/perf.json with every budget from CLAUDE.md, config/theme.json palette tokens, config/realtime.json) and copy, each validated by a zod schema with a test; central copy file with slang-pack layer (test proves swapping the pack changes rendered text); one shared formatter module: money shown as whole dollars (GR-11) and counts via Intl.NumberFormat notation 'compact' (UX-2); a copy test fails if any copy string uses a superlative (cheapest, biggest, best, most, fastest) as literal text rather than a value computed from data (GR-11); Zustand store with localStorage persistence and schema version (test for persist and rehydrate).

tasks.title: Core engine
tasks.acceptance: Pure-function game clock (1 real min = 10 game min of passive time, pauses when tab hidden, 1x/2x toggle); actions fast-forward the personal clock instantly by their duration; the engine never reads the real clock (time is injected) and exposes city time (real New York wall-clock time) separately from the personal game clock; energy, hunger, mood decay with penalties at zero; action system with time, money, energy costs and stat effects validated in the engine; save/load with a schema migration test; unit tests for time math, action fast-forward, day and week rollover, insufficient funds, and city time across a DST change.

tasks.title: Geo pipeline and projection
tasks.acceptance: npm run geo:build reproducibly downloads pinned sources (NYC Open Data borough boundaries clipped to shoreline, NYC parks, Neighborhood Tabulation Areas, MTA static GTFS subway shapes and stops; OSM only for a layer no city source provides, kept in its own ODbL file) into a gitignored cache and writes simplified, quantized layers to /data/geo plus play zones (grouped NTAs) to /data/zones; output is deterministic (checksum test: same input gives byte-identical output); raw MTA files are kept unmodified in the cache and derived files are labelled derived; /data/geo/SOURCES.md lists each source URL, retrieval date, license or terms, transformations and required attribution text (MTA: not endorsed, no accuracy claim; OSM ODbL notice if used); one projection module (lat/lng to local metres, fixed origin) is shared by scene and engine; base geo gzipped size is within perf.json geoBaseGzKB; unit tests prove known coordinates land in the correct borough (Times Square in Manhattan, the Unisphere in Queens, Prospect Park in Brooklyn, a Bronx point, St George in Staten Island), an Upper Bay point is in no borough, and every subway station lies on a line.

tasks.title: 3D city base scene
tasks.acceptance: The react-three-fiber canvas is lazy-loaded with no SSR so the DOM shell is interactive before the 3D chunk arrives; borough land extruded from /data/geo, water plane, parks, subway lines as ribbons in our own colours with plain line letters and stations as markers (no MTA logos or bullets); toon shading via a shared gradient ramp and palette tokens from config/theme.json; camera rig with one-finger pan, pinch zoom and limited two-finger rotate and tilt, bounded to the NYC extent with zoom limits; frameloop is on demand (test hook frame counter shows zero frames over 2 s idle); zero console warnings with the pinned three version (if R3F triggers three deprecation warnings, pin three to the newest version that does not and record it in progress.md); required map attribution visible on the map; a test-mode hook exposes camera state and renderer.info; Playwright pans and zooms on mobile-390 and asserts camera state; draw calls and triangles at the default view are within the mid-tier budget.

tasks.title: Quality tiers and performance budgets
tasks.acceptance: A pure tier picker chooses low, mid or high from WebGL2 support, MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE, deviceMemory, hardwareConcurrency, renderer string and Save-Data/prefers-reduced-data, with every threshold in perf.json (unit tests per signal); the runtime steps down one tier via drei PerformanceMonitor when average FPS stays below the config floor, with hysteresis, and never auto-upgrades above the detected tier; a settings override is persisted; per-tier settings (DPR cap, shadows, outlines, building density, max visible avatars) come from config; npm run budget fails when shell JS, 3D chunk JS, total JS, base geo or district assets exceed perf.json (gzipped); npm run e2e:perf runs a cold load under the cc-mid-4g profile (4 Mbps down, 1 Mbps up, 150 ms RTT, 4x CPU) on the low tier and asserts shell interactive within budget and playable within budget (median of 3 runs), a warm load within budget, and draw calls and triangles per tier; any shadow uses PCFShadowMap, never PCFSoftShadowMap.

tasks.title: Tappable places, accessible Places panel, no-WebGL fallback
tasks.acceptance: Points placed by real latitude and longitude render as instanced pins, are tappable with an on-screen hit area of at least 44 px and open a place sheet stub; a DOM Places panel lists every place grouped by borough, is fully keyboard navigable, offers the same actions as tapping in 3D and announces selection (A11Y-3); when WebGL is unavailable or the context is lost, the app shows the Places panel and a static stylised fallback and stays playable, and recovers when the context is restored; Playwright taps a point in the canvas (screen coordinates from the test hook) and the same place via the panel, and a WebGL-disabled run completes a place selection; axe passes; S07 render half (orchestrator note, approved S07 plan): pins come from src/lib/world/places.ts mapPlaces() with landmarks as placeholder markers until S07a/S07b; Bronx and Staten Island land renders dimmed per boroughRenderState with an 'expanding soon' label and teaser pins for bronx-ballpark and staten-island-ferry; the Places panel uses placeAccessibleName; a test hook reports per-borough land style and pin count; Playwright and axe prove locked places' names explain the lock.

tasks.title: District buildings
tasks.acceptance: The geo script derives low-poly building masses from NYC Open Data building footprints (roof height field) for districts listed in config (Midtown, Lower Manhattan, Downtown Brooklyn and DUMBO, Williamsburg, Long Island City, Astoria, Flushing, Jamaica), simplified and merged per district per tier; elsewhere procedural low blocks by density; rendered as merged or instanced meshes with the shared scene shading (lit by default per DEC-24/28, toon optional) and flat emissive lit windows at night; no building carries a business name; each tier stays within its district-asset, draw-call and triangle budgets (npm run budget and e2e:perf); SOURCES.md updated.

tasks.title: Day/night cycle on the personal game clock
tasks.acceptance: The 3D city's lighting follows the player's personal game clock (user decision 2026-10-07): a real-world sky (morning blue, golden hour, dusk, real night) with real-world colours on the city (DEC-26), sun direction and colour, and ambient and hemisphere light interpolate between config keyframes (dawn, day, golden hour, dusk, night) in scene.json; the scene re-evaluates lighting only when the game minute changes (frameloop stays on demand, zero idle frames); at night building windows (S04d) and streetlight and landmark accents glow with flat emissive per tier, never on the memorial; this task does not change the UI theme (S04g owns it); reduced motion steps between keyframes instead of blending; draw calls, triangles and shader programs stay within perf.json for every tier; unit tests cover keyframe interpolation at boundaries and midnight wrap; Playwright screenshots at 08:00, golden hour, 21:00 and 03:00 via a seeded clock prove the look, and the console guard passes.

tasks.title: Interface theme: real-world palette, light by day and dark glass by night
tasks.acceptance: Per DEC-26 (user decision 2026-10-07): the indigo/hot-pink palette is retired; the interface (HUD, tabs, sheets, panels, toasts, welcome card, legal pages) uses clean light frosted cards by day and dark glass by night with taxi yellow as the single brand accent, switching on the same personal game clock keyframes as S04f; both palettes are tokens in config/theme.json; the switch is driven by a data attribute on the root element set from a boot island, so the shell carries only CSS variables (shell budget holds), and pages render in the day palette until the game clock is known; every text and control colour pair meets WCAG 2.2 AA in both palettes (automated contrast test plus axe in both themes); the change cross-fades over config milliseconds and is instant under prefers-reduced-motion; no layout shift; darwin screenshot baselines for both palettes at 390 and 1280; the console guard passes.

tasks.title: Hand-made 3D asset pipeline (CC0 packs)
tasks.acceptance: Per DEC-24 (user decision 2026-10-07): a reproducible `npm run assets:build` script downloads pinned CC0 hand-made low-poly packs (each with version, URL, sha256 and licence recorded in data/assets/SOURCES.md; a test fails on any asset without a CC0/MIT licence entry, or project-original for blender-script sources (DEC-25)), selects the models listed in data/assets/catalog.json, harmonises them to the real-world model palette (DEC-26), with the shading model (lit or toon) chosen from the showcase, and writes compressed glTF (meshopt geometry; colours baked to vertex colours, textures only with approval) under public/models with a manifest hashed into the asset version; per-asset triangle and byte budgets live in perf.json and the build fails over them; runtime loading uses the pinned three/drei loaders in lazy chunks only (never the shell), with instancing for repeats and disposal on unmount; a showcase test hook renders each catalog model for screenshots at 390 and 1280; npm run budget reports model bytes per tier against the bytes-to-playable budgets and the build reports (never silently changes) any budget pressure; zero console warnings.

tasks.title: Street dressing with hand-made props
tasks.acceptance: Seeded, deterministic placement of S04h catalog props (streetlights, hydrants, benches, trees, parked taxis and cars, traffic lights, roof water towers) around the home, venues, landmarks and the camera focus along real street segments, instanced per model and tier with per-tier instance caps in perf.json (off on the low tier unless measured headroom allows), streetlights glowing at night through the shared night-glow uniform (S04f), never on or around the memorial, no text or liveries, no blocking of pins or picking (raycast off), zero idle frames; npm run budget and e2e:perf pass for every tier. Also fixes GLOW-1: Kenney commercial buildings (building-a..d) get real window glass (Blender-authored window panes or a geometric region rule) so only glass glows at night, re-enabling their night glow (disabled in the interim by S04h p2); the asset glow test is updated to include them. Amended 2026-10-08 (approved plan): props may be instanced or merged per model/chunk and tier (merged onto the district material so no new shader programs); includes fill-lite (lots, plates and trees in the block instancing beyond districts, triangle-neutral on low).

tasks.title: Real city fill
tasks.acceptance: Beyond the detailed districts, the city uses real block footprints (DOF tax blocks or LION-derived) instead of the jittered grid, with lit windows on fill at night (fixes NOTE-27; lets TUNE-16 use coarser cells or a distance fade), street ribbons, and optional mini-districts with real footprints around off-district places; deterministic geo:build; per-tier bytes, triangles and draw calls within perf.json (any budget raise is put to the user first); zero new shader programs; zero idle frames; low tier stays within its caps; screenshots compared against the competitors.

tasks.title: Offline and caching
tasks.acceptance: A Serwist service worker precaches the shell, the 3D chunk, base geo and district assets for the detected tier, with versioned caches so updates replace old data; authenticated API responses are never cached; the service worker script is served with the no-cache headers from the Next.js PWA guide; Playwright loads the map, goes offline, reloads and completes a solo action; the warm-load budget passes.

tasks.title: Guest start on the 3D map
tasks.acceptance: Opening the root URL in a fresh browser shows the shell, then the playable 3D NYC map centred on the player's Queens start within the perf.json budgets, with no signup; a player avatar placeholder stands at the start point; anonymous Supabase auth with a local-only fallback when env vars are missing (test runs with env vars absent); HUD with stats, clock, money, clout and the goal line 'Make it in New York', placed in the overlay safe zones; page title and meta use the tagline 'Tap In. Blow Up.'; Playwright test confirms.

tasks.title: Welcome card: 18+ check, consent, audio choice
tasks.acceptance: On first visit one welcome card sits over the already-loading map (the map keeps loading behind it and perf budgets still pass) with a neutral year-of-birth picker (no default, no hint of the threshold), a consent checkbox linking Terms and Privacy, and the audio choice 'Play our music' or 'I'll bring my own'; under 18 shows an in-voice 'come back when you're 18' screen, locks the gate on that device for 24 hours, and creates no Supabase user; 18+ stores attestation (boolean and timestamp, not the birth year), consent version and timestamp, and the audio choice locally; anonymous Supabase sign-in happens only after a passing attestation; the form follows the shared pattern (noValidate, one zod schema, all errors at once inline with aria-invalid and aria-describedby, focus on the first invalid field, errors recomputed on change) (GR-1, GR-2, GR-8); no AudioContext is created and no audio is requested before the audio choice (GR-13); returning players never see the card again; existing e2e specs use a shared fixture that passes the card; Playwright covers the 18+ path, the under-18 path, an empty submit and an error that is fixed.

tasks.title: Audio channels and 'My own music'
tasks.acceptance: Audio system with separate music, sfx, ambience and voice channels plus master, each with its own volume; a one-tap HUD control and a settings toggle for 'My own music' mute in-game music only while sfx and ambience keep playing, with visible now-playing state and an accessible name; the choice is remembered per device (and synced to the account in S18c) and nothing overrides it; audio unlocks only from a deliberate tap on the audio choice or the sound control (GR-13); where the browser supports it, the audio session is set to mix with other apps (for example Safari's navigator.audioSession, checked against current docs) and sfx never take over the media session; all audio assets are CC0 or otherwise licensed and listed in /data/audio/SOURCES.md, with no third-party streams; audio loads lazily after the map is playable; unit tests for mixer state; Playwright proves no audio requests before the choice and that muting music keeps sfx enabled; mixing with a background music app on real iOS and Android is listed under Needs human review.

tasks.title: Shell diet: boot path only
tasks.acceptance: The shell JS for / (npm run budget) contains only the boot path: layout, overlay shell, HUD, welcome card, persisted store and the engine modules the HUD needs; every other feature UI (event sheet, shop, place action sheet, panels, transit planner) and its data (event catalog, item catalog, transit network) loads via next/dynamic or a lazy loader on first use; player-facing copy is split into a small boot namespace bundled with the shell and per-feature namespaces loaded with their feature chunk through the existing copy() API (missing-namespace access is a typed error in tests, never a silent raw key); a test enumerates the shell chunks and fails if any feature module or feature copy namespace is reachable from the shell entry; the shell is at most perf.json shellJsGzKB minus 20 KB headroom after all merged slice tasks; first use of each lazy feature shows a loading state within the overlay system and no console warnings; existing tests stay green.

tasks.title: Guided first action and skippable tour
tasks.acceptance: A coach-mark tour over the live map (at most 6 steps, no tutorial screens, skippable, resumable from Help) leads the player through a first bodega purchase near their Queens start in about 20 seconds; a new player starts with at most 3 notifications, each meaningful (GR-9); no further gate or age check appears; Playwright completes the guided purchase and, separately, the skip and resume-from-Help path.

tasks.title: Boroughs, landmarks, and venues
tasks.acceptance: Five boroughs in data. Queens, Brooklyn, and Manhattan each have 8 invented venues with original names at plausible real coordinates (bodega, food spot, subway station, park or gym, coffee shop, thrift or boutique, club, job site). Landmarks at real coordinates with category, nameMode, and legalReviewed:false, at minimum: Brooklyn Bridge, Manhattan Bridge, Queensboro Bridge; Flatiron Building, Chrysler Building; Statue of Liberty (viewed from Battery Park), Washington Square Arch; Central Park, the High Line, Prospect Park, Flushing Meadows (Unisphere), Astoria Park; the Queens ballpark and the Brooklyn arena (generic labels); City Hall, Brooklyn Borough Hall, Queens Borough Hall; Grand Central, Penn Station, Jamaica Station; Times Square, DUMBO, Coney Island boardwalk, Flushing Main Street; 9/11 Memorial (memorial category). Landmarks show as placeholder markers in 3D until S07a and S07b. Bronx and Staten Island render as dimmed 'expanding soon' land teasing the Bronx ballpark and the Staten Island Ferry. Brooklyn and Manhattan unlock by clout level, with in-voice why-locked copy that is also in the accessible name. Validation tests: every landmark has a category and nameMode; branded names use generic labels; memorials have no flex, clout, emote, or event hooks; any superlative in venue copy is computed from data. Gating tests.

tasks.title: Low-poly landmarks I: bridges, buildings, stations, government
tasks.acceptance: Code-built low-poly models (procedural primitives, no downloaded models) in the toon style for every S07 landmark in the bridge, building, station and government categories, placed at real coordinates and orientation; generic-labelled landmarks show only their generic label; per-tier LOD via drei Detailed; per-landmark triangle budget from perf.json; merged or instanced where repeated; npm run budget and e2e:perf pass for every tier; each model is reachable from the Places panel.

tasks.title: Low-poly landmarks II: parks, monuments, stadiums, neighborhoods, memorial
tasks.acceptance: Code-built low-poly models for the remaining S07 landmarks; the Statue of Liberty is visible from Battery Park at the default zoom range; the memorial uses a muted palette with no emissive or animated effects, no emotes and no flex FX (test asserts no effect components are attached); per-tier LOD and triangle budgets as S07a; npm run budget and e2e:perf pass for every tier.

tasks.title: NYC landmark models built in Blender
tasks.acceptance: Per DEC-25 (user decision 2026-10-07): every S07 landmark gets an original hand-made-style low-poly model authored by a committed, reproducible Blender Python script under scripts/blender/ (run headless with a pinned Blender version recorded in README; output byte-stable for the same inputs), built from real measurements recorded with sources in data/landmarks/SOURCES.md, coloured in real-world colours (DEC-26), with per-tier LODs, exported as glTF and processed through the S04h pipeline within per-landmark triangle and byte budgets in perf.json; trademark-sensitive landmarks stay generic (no logos, signage or text; LEGAL-1); the memorial stays muted with no emissive; models replace the code-built stand-ins at their real coordinates and headings (frames.derived.json) with the code-built kit as fallback; a showcase renders each landmark for screenshot review at 390 and 1280; npm run budget and e2e:perf pass for every tier.

tasks.title: Transit and rush hour
tasks.acceptance: Walk, subway, and taxi with time and cost computed from real distances between points, per-mode speeds and fares in config; subway trips route via the nearest stations on the real lines in /data/geo, with walking legs at each end; travel fast-forwards the personal clock while the avatar animates along the route in 3D (subway along its ribbon) for at most the config animation length, and users with prefers-reduced-motion get an instant cut; rush hour (7-10am, 4-7pm) slows subway and drains mood; random MTA delay event hook; no MTA logos or official line bullets; unit tests for distance, routing, and modifiers.

tasks.title: Location action sheet, club door, landmark visits
tasks.acceptance: Tapping a venue or landmark in 3D or choosing it in the Places panel opens the same action sheet filtered by personal time of day and opening hours; closed venues show opening time; the club opens at night with a cover charge, a minimum clout level at the door with in-voice refusal copy, and a clout gain inside; non-memorial landmarks have a Visit action (time cost, mood gain) and a flexMultiplier from config for use by S13; memorials show a respectful info card only; tests.

tasks.title: Items, inventory, and shop
tasks.acceptance: 12 clothing and makeup items across 3 rarity tiers and 5 slots plus 3 gift types, all with currency 'cash', price, rarity, sellValue, cloutValue, statEffects; gifts are consumed when used on NPCs or yourself and cannot target another player; inventory and outfit equip; buy and sell with depreciation, prices displayed via the shared money formatter; schema validation and unit tests including insufficient funds.

tasks.title: Jobs and rent
tasks.acceptance: Four jobs per CLAUDE.md anchors (barista, retail, delivery with higher energy cost, junior dev gated by clout level with why-locked copy) with 4-hour shifts that fast-forward the personal clock; rent due every 7 game days; missed rent escalates to eviction and a move to cheaper housing; housing copy that compares rents is computed from data (GR-11); unit tests.

tasks.title: Shop, jobs and rent UI in place sheets
tasks.acceptance: Inside the S09 location action sheet (lazy-loaded per DEC-11): boutique and thrift venues show a shop listing every for-sale item with copy name, slot, rarity, price via formatMoney and a Buy button whose disabled state explains why (owned, can't afford: shortfall) in its accessible name; an inventory panel reachable from the HUD lists owned wearables and gifts with Equip/Unequip, Sell (showing the current resale value) and Use on yourself; job-site and other job venues offer Work a shift for each job they list, with locked jobs showing the why-locked copy in the button's accessible name and an out-of-energy state; rent status (next due day, amount owed, last rent notice) shows in a HUD or phone panel using the S11 copy helpers; every action goes through the store and shows the engine's outcome or typed error in voice; all controls are native, 44 px targets, axe-clean, inside the overlay system (UX-1); Playwright on mobile-390 and desktop-1280 buys an item, equips it, sells it, works a shift and sees cash and clock change, and sees a rent payment notice after advancing past a rent day via a test hook.

tasks.title: Economy simulation test
tasks.acceptance: A scripted bot plays 30 game days solo with a sensible strategy and ends neither bankrupt nor wildly rich (bounds in test); it saves roughly $150 per week and reaches the first apartment upgrade affordability between game days 10 and 14; any cost tuning needed to hit this is done in /data/config and logged; the bot also records its maximum clout and cash gain per action and per game day into a fixture used by S18c plausibility ceilings; test fails if balance drifts.

tasks.title: Explore: filters, search, happening now
tasks.acceptance: Category chips (coffee, food, parks, landmarks, nightlife, culture, job sites) and text search over the Places panel, keyboard accessible; a 'Happening now' chip listing S34 live events with countdown (shown once S34 lands); the map pin filter mirrors the panel; lazy chunk within shell and perf budgets (DEC-11). Engine stays pure; data/config/copy in /data; grants only via the grant function (ECON-1); player-to-player cash and items only through the server-authoritative player economy (S56, DEC-38); the S12 bot still meets its targets; axe clean, 44 px targets, GR-1/2/8 form rules where forms exist; within perf.json budgets (lazy chunks, shell untouched).

tasks.title: Clout, style, flex, levels
tasks.acceptance: Integer clout from item cloutValue (counts only while owned or equipped; a buy/sell loop cannot farm clout, proven by test), first paycheck, and a flex action with seeded-random viral chance weighted by outfit style score and the landmark flexMultiplier when flexing at a landmark; style score multiplies clout gains; six levels (Nobody, Local, Scene Regular, Known, Famous, Icon) in config with HUD progress; a level-up event is emitted; every clout change writes a typed ledger entry (source, amount, currency) so premium items (S25) plug in and can be capped and S18c can check plausibility without engine changes; unit tests.

tasks.title: Events
tasks.acceptance: Data-driven event engine with conditions (time, borough, location, stats, clout, items), weights, and choice outcomes; modal UI in the overlay system; 15 events in the voice of CLAUDE.md including MTA delay, rent hike, free pizza, club promoter offer, viral moment, 2 mild crime events, and at least 2 landmark-tied events; validation tests prove no event can fire at a memorial, no crime event can fire at a government building, and no event rewards or requires drinking or references drugs or sexual content; seeded-random tests.

tasks.title: Goals, grants, Icon moment, prestige
tasks.acceptance: Goals screen (first paycheck, first outfit, first landmark visit, first club night, first friend, level thresholds) with rewards and progress; every reward goes through one grant function that is idempotent (grant key), audited (grant log), eligibility-targeted and capped relative to the next progression goal from config, and granted value never counts toward goal progress (ECON-1, tests); reaching Icon shows a victory screen with a share hook and a prestige option (restart progress, keep cosmetics and premium items, earn a prestige badge; rules in config); tests; for players without a session, grants are local only and are re-validated by S18c when a session exists.

tasks.title: 3D apartment and decor
tasks.acceptance: A low-poly toon 3D apartment interior for the Queens room and the Brooklyn 1BR upgrade (higher rent, more slots), within per-tier budgets; 6 decor items across rarity tiers placed in slots by tapping in 3D or through an equivalent DOM slot list (A11Y-3); colour variants have human-readable names (A11Y-1); locked upgrades show in-voice why-locked copy, also in the accessible name; home score feeds clout; Playwright places an item both ways.

tasks.title: 3D avatar and 'Make it you' creator
tasks.acceptance: A modular low-poly 3D avatar (code-built or CC0 parts listed in SOURCES.md) within per-tier triangle budgets, used on the map and in the apartment; guests start immediately with a randomized avatar and never meet the creator before first play; after the first action the creator is offered (skippable, always reachable from the HUD) with the flow Look, Traits, Dream (career path: influencer, streamer, artist/DJ, founder/hustler), Neighborhood roll (dice reveal among Queens start neighborhoods), Home; option and roll copy is generated from the same data that drives the options (GR-10); Hair, Facial hair, Accessories, Skin and Outfit are separate categories (GR-12); every swatch has a human colour name (A11Y-1); career path sets the goal line copy and a path-tagged bonus from config, and the S12 bot meets its targets for every path; native controls clicked in e2e; tests.

tasks.title: Needs, moodlets and working home objects
tasks.acceptance: Six needs in /data/config (DEC-40): energy, hunger, fun, social, hygiene and bladder (bladder handled by home objects and venue restrooms, never humiliating); decay on the personal game clock only, pausing while hidden and never draining while away (GR-20). Moodlets from /data with source, size and game-minute expiry, listed with plain numbers in a 'Why you feel this way' sheet. Home objects work: fridge/stove (eat, cook from a pantry), bed (sleep), shower (hygiene), desk/guitar (skill hooks for S39), each usable by tapping in 3D or from an equivalent DOM list (A11Y-3). Groceries bought at bodegas; home delivery costs a fee. Optional 'Free will' setting (off by default) uses one home object when a need is critical, spending at most a config amount. No humiliating moodlet or event; nightlife moodlets never come from drinking. Unit tests: decay, hidden pause, stacking, expiry; S12 bot meets targets with needs on. Engine stays pure; data/config/copy in /data; grants only via the grant function (ECON-1); player-to-player cash and items only through the server-authoritative player economy (S56, DEC-38); the S12 bot still meets its targets; axe clean, 44 px targets, GR-1/2/8 form rules where forms exist; within perf.json budgets (lazy chunks, shell untouched).

tasks.title: Daily Drop riddle hunt
tasks.acceptance: Each New York day one riddle (copy generated from place data, GR-10) points to a non-memorial, non-government landmark or venue, seeded and server-chosen when online. Up to two hints unlock at config city times. 'Search here' costs a little energy with a config daily attempt cap. Every finder gets the same capped cash and clout grant; early finders get only a cosmetic badge tier. Finder counts come from real server finds only (UX-3). Offline it runs on device time and rewards are re-validated by S18c. Tests: memorial exclusion, grant idempotency, attempt cap, city-time rollover across DST. Engine stays pure; data/config/copy in /data; grants only via the grant function (ECON-1); player-to-player cash and items only through the server-authoritative player economy (S56, DEC-38); the S12 bot still meets its targets; axe clean, 44 px targets, GR-1/2/8 form rules where forms exist; within perf.json budgets (lazy chunks, shell untouched).

tasks.title: Wishes and Perks
tasks.acceptance: Three rotating wishes drawn from /data with conditions; swapping one costs perk points.
